Phase 31 implementation submitted for review. Plan: docs/phases/headless-turn-engine-30-arc.md (approved r3). Findings: docs/phases/headless-turn-engine-findings.md. Commits since plan approval: b1b8733 (core), e39aa91 (Windows lock, CI, SKILL/README), dafa837 (findings/roadmap).

What was built (files):
- tagteam/headless.py (new, ~900 lines): Adapter table (CLAUDE: `-p --output-format stream-json --verbose` + defaults `--permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools Bash Read Edit Write Glob Grep`; CODEX: `exec --json -C <root>` + defaults `--sandbox workspace-write -c approval_policy=never`, tail `--skip-git-repo-check -`); `validate_user_args`/`build_argv` structural validation (option table with arity, reserved families on normalized names, `--flag=value` and `-Cdir` forms, overridable families drop defaults, marker always last); `parse_start_command` (exact `/handoff start <slug>[ impl]`, slug alphabet); `compose_prompt` with `{boundary_clause}` for impl starts; `run_process` (stdin feed thread, separate stdout→`<stem>.events.jsonl` and rendered+`[stderr]`→`<stem>.log`, per-line flush, `start_new_session`/`CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` + `killpg`/`taskkill /T` on timeout and Ctrl-C); `snapshot_identity`/`verify_transition` (pre-spawn identity, start-command targets, expected role/action/round + state phase/type/round/seq/updated_by checks); pause marker read/write/clear; `HeadlessEngine` (validate/roles/argv, run_owed_turn, usage row incl. failed turns, `headless_usage_unparsed` + `headless_turn_failed` diagnostics, notify); `tail_command`; log pruning (newest 50).
- tagteam/db.py: SCHEMA_VERSION 3, additive `usage` table + index, `add_usage`/`get_usage`; `_migrate` tolerates newer user_version.
- tagteam/cycle.py: `tail_rounds()`; `cycle rounds --tail N` (>=1, else error).
- tagteam/config.py: `agents.<role>.headless.{provider,executable,args}` in validate_config (types, unknown provider, args must be list of strings, unknown keys) + fallback parser; `infer_headless_provider`, `get_headless_spec`.
- tagteam/watcher.py: `--mode headless` (rejected by auto-detect: `_auto_detect_mode` unchanged, test added), `--turn-timeout`, `--tail-rounds`; `_StateProcessor(engine=)`; headless branch in `_handle_ready` (blocking spawn); tick() short-circuits the watchdog re-send in headless and logs pause state; poll trigger forced; startup validation exit 1; banner shows adapters/pause; `watch()` now returns bool so `watch_command` exits 1 on startup failure.
- tagteam/cli.py: `tagteam tail`, help text.
- tagteam/dualwrite.py: DISCOVERED DEPENDENCY — module-level `import fcntl` meant every cycle/state write failed on Windows since Phase 28; replaced with a portable `_os_lock/_os_unlock` (fcntl on POSIX, msvcrt.locking on win32). Required for the Windows criterion (a headless agent must be able to `cycle add`).
- .github/workflows/tests.yml (new): pytest on ubuntu-latest + windows-latest. Not yet pushed (Jack pushes) — status pending.
- SKILL.md (both copies, now identical — the shipped copy had drifted and lacked the AMEND paragraph): `--tail N`, headless-turns note, `/handoff start [phase] impl` = implement first / init exactly once.
- README: "Headless mode (opt-in)" section, Windows guidance, CLI reference. docs/roadmap.md Phase 31 status.
- tests: tests/test_headless.py (96 tests: argv rejections/acceptance for both adapters, provider inference, config validation, executable resolution, engine validate errors, start-command parsing, boundary clause, parsers against real captured fixtures tests/fixtures/headless/{claude,codex}_stream.jsonl, verify_transition cases incl. unrelated seq advance / wrong round / wrong cycle / AMEND / state mismatch / cross-phase & plan→impl start targets / malformed start command; e2e via tests/fixtures/fake_agent.py installed on PATH as claude/codex (POSIX script or Windows .cmd): reviewer→lead ok, no_round pause+no-dispatch+restart+clear, nonzero, timeout with grandchild kill, log-grows-before-exit + stderr separation, malformed usage → null row + diagnostic, wrong round, impl-start boundary e2e ok/no_round, prune; watcher integration: engine dispatch + no watchdog resend, done doesn't send, auto-detect, watch_command exit codes, paused banner; tail command; cycle rounds --tail; schema v3 fresh/v2→v3, newer user_version tolerated, add/get usage). Full suite: 674 passed, 4 skipped; existing test_watcher*/test_config tests unmodified.

Real-CLI dogfood (details + numbers in findings doc): step-0 probes captured; scratch project ran plan-approved → `/handoff start greet-cli impl` → headless Claude implemented + inited impl r1 (39 s, ok) → headless Codex reviewed + APPROVED (73 s, ok); usage rows recorded; `tagteam tail` followed the live turn. Downgrade proof done: 0.7.1 opens/reads/writes the v3 project. THIS reviewer turn is dogfood item (a): it is being spawned by `tagteam watch --mode headless` on this repo.

Deviations / notes for review: (1) `--turn-retries` intentionally absent (plan r2). (2) codex `model` is null in usage (not in its event stream). (3) Windows CI not yet run (needs a push); real Windows CLI smoke not performed — stated in findings. (4) `tagteam upgrade` in the revert recipe is registry-wide (idempotent) — noted in findings. (5) `snapshot_identity` uses expected round = state.round+1 for lead ordinary turns and state.round for reviewer turns, matching cycle.add_round semantics.

Blocking changes requested.

1. Headless startup silently accepts invalid headless config. `_build_processor()` never calls `validate_config()`, while `get_headless_spec()` coerces a non-list `headless.args` to `[]` and `infer_headless_provider()` falls through from an explicit unknown provider to command/name inference. I reproduced both `args: "--model opus"` and `provider: gemini` (with `name: Claude`) producing `HeadlessEngine.validate() == []` and launching the Claude adapter. This directly fails the success criterion that `--mode headless` exit 1 for args that are not a list and for unknown providers. Preserve/report the invalid raw values or run strict config validation in the startup path; an explicit invalid provider must not fall back. Add watch/startup-level regression tests for both cases, not only unit tests of `validate_config()`.

2. `.tagteam/turns/inflight.json` never contains the spawned PID required by the plan: `run_owed_turn()` writes `"pid": null` before calling `run_process()`, and `run_process()` never reports the `Popen.pid` back. Refactor/update the pointer immediately after spawn and add a mid-run assertion that `pid` is a live integer, while retaining cleanup on exit/Ctrl-C.

3. Spawn failures escape the engine instead of becoming a recorded, paused failure. `resolve_executable()` accepts any existing configured path (including a directory/non-executable), `subprocess.Popen()` is outside any handling that creates a `TurnResult`, and the `finally` only removes `inflight.json`; therefore `PermissionError`/`OSError` yields no usage row, `headless_turn_failed` diagnostic, pause marker, or notification. Validate configured paths as runnable where possible and catch spawn-time `OSError`, mapping it to a documented failure outcome (or explicitly add one) with the same usage/diagnostic/pause guarantees. Add an engine-level regression test.

4. Outcome verification does not implement the approved per-cycle status check. `verify_transition()` matches a new action entry and top-level state fields, but never verifies the target cycle's `state`, `ready_for`, and `round` correspond to that action. The plan explicitly requires those checks, including `ready_for: reviewer` after lead submit and the action-specific reviewer state. Add the status validation and tamper/concurrency regression tests so a matching entry plus stale/corrupt cycle status is `no_round`.

5. Close or explicitly resolve the remaining gating acceptance items before approval: Windows CI is still documented as pending and has not run because the commits are unpushed; findings item (a) remains `_filled in below_` despite this headless review turn; item (b), the Phase 32 plan-cycle dogfood, remains pending; and the planned 0.8.0 version/tag/release criterion is not satisfied (`pyproject.toml` is still 0.7.1). If release/tagging is intentionally post-approval or Phase 32 dogfood is intentionally deferred, update the approved plan/findings to state the revised gate instead of submitting with contradictory unchecked criteria.

Verification performed: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` -> 674 passed, 4 skipped. The green suite does not cover items 1-4 above.

Round 2 (commit c27543d): all five blocking items addressed. Suite: 682 passed, 4 skipped.

1. Strict headless config at startup — `HeadlessEngine.validate()` now runs `validate_config()` first and treats any error as fatal (returns before building roles); `infer_headless_provider()` returns an explicit provider verbatim (never falls back to command/name inference), so `provider: gemini` errors as "unknown headless provider 'gemini'"; `get_headless_spec()` passes non-list `args` through raw so `build_argv` rejects them ("must be a list of strings"). New parametrized test `test_engine_and_watch_reject_invalid_headless_config` covers `args: "--model opus"`, `provider: gemini`, `executable: 42`, unknown key — each asserts engine errors, no role built, AND `watch_command(["--mode","headless"]) == 1` with resolvable fake CLIs on PATH (startup-level, as requested).

2. PID in `inflight.json` — `run_process()` takes `on_spawn(pid)` and calls it immediately after a successful Popen; the engine rewrites `inflight.json` with the live pid. The log-grows test now samples `inflight.json` mid-run and asserts an integer pid is present and stable; cleanup on exit/Ctrl-C unchanged (new `test_ctrl_c_kills_child_and_clears_inflight` also asserts the child + grandchild are dead and inflight is gone).

3. Spawn failures — `resolve_executable()` requires configured paths to exist, be a file, and be executable (`os.access X_OK`; directory/non-exec/non-string rejected — tests added). `run_process()` wraps Popen: `OSError` → `SpawnError`; the engine maps it to a new documented outcome `spawn_failed` (added to `db.USAGE_STATUSES`) with the same guarantees as other failures: usage row (`status=spawn_failed`, exit_code null), `headless_turn_failed` diagnostic, pause marker, notification, `[tagteam] spawn failed:` in the log, inflight removed. Engine-level test `test_spawn_failure_is_recorded_and_pauses` (Popen patched to raise PermissionError).

4. Per-cycle status verification — `verify_transition()` now reads the target cycle's status and requires `(state, ready_for)` to match the matched action (SUBMIT_FOR_REVIEW → in-progress/reviewer; APPROVE → approved/None; REQUEST_CHANGES → in-progress/lead or escalated/human for auto-escalation; ESCALATE → escalated/human; NEED_HUMAN → needs-human/human) and `status.round == target_round`, before the top-level state checks. Tamper tests: `test_matching_entry_but_tampered_cycle_status_is_not_ok` (ready_for flipped, state approved, round corrupted → no_round with reason naming the mismatch) and `test_lead_submit_requires_ready_for_reviewer`.

5. Gates — resolved explicitly rather than left contradictory: (i) findings §(a) now records THIS cycle's r1 headless Codex review (205.8 s, 1.69M in / 7.5k out / 1.56M cache-read, ok → REQUEST_CHANGES) and the pause-marker manual hold; (ii) plan Success Criteria are ticked where satisfied and three are annotated with revised gates: Windows CI green **gates the v0.8.0 tag push** (workflow committed; first run happens on Jack's push — lead has commit-only permission), Scope 9(b) Phase 32 plan-cycle dogfood is a **soak-period item** (only possible after 0.8.0 ships and soaks per proposal §5), and the 0.8.0 **release/tag is a post-approval step** — `pyproject.toml` is now bumped to 0.8.0 in this commit so the release is bump→(approve)→tag. Plan status boxes updated. Also added the Ctrl-C test so that ticked criterion is backed by a test.

Note: this round's reviewer turn is again spawned headless by `tagteam watch --mode headless` on this repo; the interactive lead holds a pause marker during it so no second Claude is spawned into the working tree.

Two blocking changes remain after review. Verification: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` -> 682 passed, 4 skipped; `git diff --check` is clean.

1. The spawn-failure behavior is implemented, but the claimed "new documented outcome `spawn_failed`" is not actually documented in the approved contract or user-facing failure docs. `docs/phases/headless-turn-engine-30-arc.md` still defines `usage.status` as only `ok | timeout | nonzero_exit | no_round`, says "Everything else" is one of those three failures, and its Failure handling table has no spawn-failure row. `README.md` likewise lists only timeout, nonzero exit, and no round. Either map `Popen` `OSError` to an existing documented status (most naturally `nonzero_exit`) or explicitly add `spawn_failed` everywhere the outcome/status vocabulary and recovery behavior are specified. Add an assertion that the documented status vocabulary stays aligned with `db.USAGE_STATUSES` if practical.

2. Strict startup validation is still bypassed by the repository's supported no-PyYAML fallback parser. Reproduction against current code:

```
_read_config_fallback('agents:\n  lead:\n    name: Claude\n    headless:\n      args: "--model opus"\n  reviewer:\n    name: Codex\n')
```

returns `headless.args == []`, so `validate_config()` returns no errors. An unknown headless key is silently discarded the same way. The new startup regression tests exercise only the PyYAML path. Preserve invalid scalar `args` and unknown keys (or return a parse/config error) in `_read_config_fallback`, then add forced-`HAS_YAML=False` startup-level regressions for scalar `args`, unknown provider, and unknown key. This keeps the explicit optional-parser path from silently launching with different semantics.

Non-blocking test tightening while touching this area: the new PID test proves that an integer was observed, but does not perform the requested live-process assertion. Check `_pid_alive(pid)` during the sampler's in-flight window so the test pins both integer shape and liveness.
